Algebra I · Lesson 4.1

What an Equation Says

Solve this lesson →All lessons

An equation joins two expressions with an equals sign and claims they have the same value. That makes it a different kind of object from everything in chapters 1 through 3. An expression has a value. An equation makes a statement, and a statement can be true or false. Start by judging a few.

Problem
Each equation below makes a claim. 7+8=153⋅6=2140−13=27728=87+8=153⋅6=2140−13=27872​=8 Check each one by computing its left side. Enter how many of the four claims are true.
Show a hint
  • Work out each left side and compare it to the number on the right. The claim is true only when they match exactly.
  • 3⋅63⋅6 is 1818, not 2121, so that claim is false. Settle the other three the same way.
Show the full solution
7+8=157+8=15 and 40−13=2740−13=27 are true, while 3⋅63⋅6 is 1818, not 2121, and 72÷872÷8 is 99, not 88. So 22​ of the four claims are true. Writing an equation down does not make it true. The symbols make the claim, and arithmetic settles it.
Key idea
An equation is a claim. An equation is a statement that two expressions have the same value. An expression has a value, but an equation is true or false. 7+8=157+8=15 is true and 3⋅6=213⋅6=21 is false, and both are equations. The equals sign is not an instruction to compute, and it does not mean the answer comes next. The expression before the sign is the equation's left side, the one after it is its right side, and the claim is that the two sides have the same value, which also means they can trade places. 15=7+815=7+8 makes exactly the claim that 7+8=157+8=15 makes.
Problem
To compute 7×8+67×8+6, a student writes 7×8=56+6=627×8=56+6=62. The final number is right, but the first equals sign makes a false claim. It says 7×87×8 equals 56+656+6. Enter the difference between those two values.
Show a hint
  • Read the chain literally. Everything left of the first equals sign is one side of its claim, and everything between the two equals signs is the other.
  • The false claim is 7×8=56+67×8=56+6, so compare 5656 with 6262.
Show the full solution
The first equals sign claims 7×8=56+67×8=56+6, which says 56=6256=62. The difference is 62−56=662−56=6​. Every equals sign in a line makes its own claim, so a running chain of them asserts things you never meant. Write the steps on separate lines instead.

Every claim so far could be settled outright because both sides were numbers. Put a variable in and that changes. n+3=10n+3=10 is true if nn is 77 and false if nn is anything else, so the equation is not simply true or false. Its truth depends on the value of the variable.

Problem
Consider the equation 5n+8=435n+8=43. Substitute n=5n=5, n=6n=6, and n=7n=7 in turn, evaluating the left side each time. One of the three values makes the claim true. Enter it.
Show a hint
  • Replace nn with each value and work out 5n+85n+8. You want the value that makes the left side come out to 4343.
  • At n=5n=5 the left side is 3333, and each step of 11 in nn adds 55 more.
Show the full solution
At n=5n=5 the left side is 3333, at n=6n=6 it is 3838, and at n=7n=7 it is 5⋅7+8=435⋅7+8=43, which matches the right side. The claim is true at n=7n=7​ and false at the other two.
Key idea
Solutions. A value of the variable that makes an equation true is called a solution of the equation. Substituting a solution turns the two sides into the same number. An equation with a variable is not true or false on its own. It becomes one or the other each time the variable is given a value, so the equation acts as a test that every number either passes or fails. To solve an equation means to find all of its solutions, not just one.
Problem
A student claims y=6y=6 is a solution of 4y−7=2y+54y−7=2y+5. Check the claim by substituting 66 for yy on each side and evaluating the two sides separately. Both come out to the same number. Enter it.
Show a hint
  • Treat the two sides as two separate expressions and evaluate each at y=6y=6, the way 1.6 evaluated expressions.
  • The left side is 4⋅6−74⋅6−7. Compute it, then compute 2⋅6+52⋅6+5 and compare.
Show the full solution
The left side is 4⋅6−7=174⋅6−7=17 and the right side is 2⋅6+5=172⋅6+5=17. Both sides equal 1717​, so the claim is true at y=6y=6 and 66 is a solution. A check evaluates each side on its own and only compares the results at the end.
Problem
The same student claims w=3w=3 is a solution of 4w+3=2w+194w+3=2w+19. Substitute w=3w=3 and evaluate both sides. They do not match. Enter how much larger the right side is than the left.
Show a hint
  • Evaluate 4w+34w+3 and 2w+192w+19 separately at w=3w=3, then subtract the smaller result from the larger.
  • The left side comes out to 1515. Now evaluate the right side and take the difference.
Show the full solution
At w=3w=3 the left side is 4⋅3+3=154⋅3+3=15 and the right side is 2⋅3+19=252⋅3+19=25, so the right side is larger by 25−15=1025−15=10​. The mismatch means w=3w=3 is not a solution, and one failed check settles that completely. The equation does have a solution, since checking w=8w=8 gives 3535 on both sides.
Key idea
Checking a value. To test whether a value is a solution, substitute it for the variable everywhere it appears, evaluate each side as its own expression, and compare the two results. Equal results mean the value is a solution, unequal results mean it is not, and there is no third outcome. Keep the substitution rules from 1.6, parentheses around negative values especially. A check is complete proof for the one value tested, but it says nothing about any other value, so a check can confirm a solution without telling you whether more exist.
Problem
One of x=−2x=−2 and x=−5x=−5 is a solution of x2−3x=10x2−3x=10. Check each candidate, keeping every substitution inside parentheses. Enter the one that works.
Show a hint
  • Evaluate x2−3xx2−3x at each candidate. Written out with parentheses, the first check is (−2)2−3(−2)(−2)2−3(−2).
  • Watch the second term. Subtracting 33 times a negative number adds a positive amount.
Show the full solution
At x=−2x=−2 the left side is (−2)2−3(−2)=4+6=10(−2)2−3(−2)=4+6=10, which matches. At x=−5x=−5 it is (−5)2−3(−5)=25+15=40(−5)2−3(−5)=25+15=40, which does not. The solution is x=−2x=−2​. It is not the only one. x=5x=5 gives 25−15=1025−15=10 as well, so this equation has two solutions, and a check can confirm one without ruling out others.

So far the equations tested have had one solution, or two. Those are not the only possibilities. An equation can also have no solutions at all, or be true for every value of its variable. The next two problems build one of each kind, and both kinds keep showing up for the rest of the course.

Problem
Try to find a solution of m+10=m+2m+10=m+2. Substitute a few values of mm and evaluate both sides. Whatever you pick, the left side exceeds the right side by the same fixed amount. Enter that amount.
Show a hint
  • Try m=1m=1, then m=5m=5. Compare the two sides each time and watch the gap between them.
  • At m=1m=1 the sides are 1111 and 33. The gap cannot depend on mm, since both sides grow by the same amount when mm does.
Show the full solution
Both sides contain the same mm, so the comparison is really between the 1010 and the 22 added to it. The left side is always larger by 10−2=810−2=8​. No value of mm can close that gap, so the equation has no solutions. That is a legitimate outcome, since the equation makes a claim and the claim happens to be false for every value.
Problem
Now try 3(t+4)=3t+123(t+4)=3t+12. Test all four values t=−6t=−6, t=0t=0, t=2t=2, and t=9t=9. Enter how many of the four make the equation true.
Show a hint
  • Evaluate the two sides separately at each value, parentheses around −6−6 included.
  • At t=0t=0 both sides are 1212 and at t=2t=2 both are 1818. Keep going, and think about what 2.1 says about these two sides.
Show the full solution
All four values work. At t=−6,0,2,9t=−6,0,2,9 both sides come out to −6,12,18,39−6,12,18,39, so the count is 44​. No luck is involved. By the distributive property from 2.1, 3(t+4)3(t+4) and 3t+123t+12 are the same expression in two forms, so the equation is true for every value of tt, not just these four.
Key idea
How many solutions. An equation can have one solution, several, none, or all of them. 5n+8=435n+8=43 is true only at n=7n=7. x2−3x=10x2−3x=10 is true at −2−2 and at 55. m+10=m+2m+10=m+2 is true nowhere, and 3(t+4)=3t+123(t+4)=3t+12 is true for every value of tt. An equation of that last kind is called an identity, and every rewrite in chapters 1 through 3 produced one, two forms of the same expression joined by an equals sign. Solving an equation means finding every solution, so a complete answer can be one number, a list, no solutions at all, or every number.

Testing values proved everything so far, and testing values has a limit. A check can confirm a solution you already suspect, but it cannot by itself find one, and it cannot promise that none were missed. The last three problems push guessing as far as it goes and show where it stops working.

Problem
The equation 9x+7=529x+7=52 is true for exactly one value of xx. You do not need to find that value yet. Read the structure of the left side and decide what the term 9x9x must equal for the equation to hold. Enter that number.
Show a hint
  • The left side is a sum of two parts, 9x9x and 77, and together they must reach 5252.
  • Whatever the 77 does not cover, the 9x9x part must make up. How far is 77 from 5252?
Show the full solution
The left side adds 77 to the term 9x9x, and the total has to be 5252. The part the 77 does not cover is 52−752−7, so 9x=459x=45​. Whichever number xx is, nine copies of it must total 4545. Lesson 4.2 turns this kind of reading into a method that finds xx every time.
Problem
Whole-number guesses fail on 6x+5=86x+5=8. x=0x=0 leaves the left side at 55 and x=1x=1 pushes it to 1111, so any solution sits between them. Of the candidates 1331​, 1221​, and 3223​, enter the one that is a solution.
Show a hint
  • Substitute each candidate into the left side and see which one makes it 88.
  • At x=12x=21​ the first term is 6⋅12=36⋅21​=3.
Show the full solution
Checking x=12x=21​ gives 6⋅12+5=3+5=86⋅21​+5=3+5=8, a true claim, so the solution is 1221​​. The other candidates fail, since x=13x=31​ makes the left side 77 and x=32x=23​ makes it 1414. Solutions are not required to be whole numbers, so guessing whole numbers cannot be the whole story.
Problem
One more, with the variable on both sides. Exactly one of a=7a=7, a=11a=11, and a=15a=15 is a solution of 2a+11=3a2a+11=3a. Check each candidate on both sides and enter the one that works.
Show a hint
  • Substitute each candidate into both sides separately, the way every check in this lesson has run.
  • At a=7a=7 the sides are 2525 and 2121. Keep going up the list.
Show the full solution
At a=7a=7 the sides are 2525 and 2121, no match. At a=11a=11 both sides equal 3333, a match. At a=15a=15 they are 4141 and 4545, no match. The solution is a=11a=11​. Equations with the variable on both sides check exactly like any other, and 4.3 studies them directly.
Fun fact
The equals sign is younger than the claim it makes. Robert Recorde introduced it in 1557 in The Whetstone of Witte, choosing a pair of parallel lines bicause noe 2 thynges can be moare equalle.

An equation claims its two sides have the same value, a solution is a value of the variable that makes the claim true, and substitution can check any candidate. What checking cannot do is produce the solutions in the first place. 4.2 builds the tool for that, moves that trade an equation for a simpler one with exactly the same solutions.

Practice these ideas

Practice
For the equation 5x−6=375x−6=37, evaluate the left side at x=7x=7.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 5⋅7−6=35−6=295⋅7−6=35−6=29​. The right side says 3737, so the two sides disagree at x=7x=7 and the claim is false there.
Practice
One of the values 22, 55, 99 is a solution of x+8=13x+8=13. Enter it.
Show the solution
Checking x=5x=5 gives 5+8=135+8=13, a true claim, so the solution is 55​. The other candidates give 1010 and 1717, and both of those claims are false.
Practice
Enter the solution of x−9=14x−9=14.
Show the solution
The equation says xx is 99 more than 1414, so x=23x=23​. Substituting back gives 23−9=1423−9=14, which is true, so 2323 really is the solution.
Practice
Enter the solution of 6x=546x=54.
Show the solution
Six copies of 99 total 5454, and substituting confirms 6⋅9=546⋅9=54, so x=9x=9​.
Practice
For 8x+7=318x+7=31, evaluate left side minus right side at x=3x=3.
Show the solution
At x=3x=3 the left side is 8⋅3+7=318⋅3+7=31, and 31−31=031−31=0​. A difference of 00 means the sides agree, so 33 is a solution of the equation.
Practice
For 2x+9=252x+9=25, evaluate left side minus right side at x=7x=7.
Show the solution
At x=7x=7 the left side is 2⋅7+9=232⋅7+9=23, and 23−25=−223−25=−2​. The difference is not 00, so 77 is not a solution, the left side lands 22 short of the right.
Practice
How many of the values 11, 22, 33, 44 are solutions of 5x−3=125x−3=12?
Show the solution
The left side comes out 22, 77, 1212, 1717 at x=1,2,3,4x=1,2,3,4, and only x=3x=3 matches the right side, so 11​ of the values is a solution.
Practice
Exactly one of 11, 22, 33 is a solution of 7x+6=277x+6=27. Enter it.
Show the solution
Checking x=3x=3 gives 7⋅3+6=277⋅3+6=27, a match, so the solution is 33​. The candidates 11 and 22 give 1313 and 2020, both short of the right side.
Practice
Enter the solution of x+9=5x+9=5.
Show the solution
The check −4+9=5−4+9=5 comes out true, so x=−4x=−4​. Nothing in the definition of a solution requires it to be positive, a solution is any value that makes the claim true.
Practice
For 10x+1=1610x+1=16, evaluate the left side at x=32x=23​.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 10⋅32+1=15+1=1610⋅23​+1=15+1=16​. That matches the right side, so 3223​ is a solution. Solutions are not required to be whole numbers.
Practice
Enter the solution of 4x=104x=10 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Four copies of 5225​ total 202=10220​=10, so the check passes and x=52x=25​​. No whole number works here, but the equation still has exactly one solution.
Practice
How many of the values −4−4, 00, 33, 1010 are solutions of 6(x+7)=6x+426(x+7)=6x+42?
Show the solution
Every check passes. At x=−4x=−4 both sides are 1818, at 00 both are 4242, at 33 both are 6060, and at 1010 both are 102102, so the count is 44​. Distributing explains it, 6(x+7)6(x+7) expands to 6x+426x+42, so the two sides are equivalent expressions and the claim is true for every value of xx.
Practice
How many of the values −3−3, 00, 88 are solutions of x=x+7x=x+7?
Show the solution
The checks give −3−3 against 44, then 00 against 77, then 88 against 1515, all false, so the count is 00​. The right side is always 77 more than the left, so no number anywhere makes this claim true. An equation can have no solutions at all.
Practice
How many of the values 00, 11, 22 are solutions of 7(x+2)=7x+27(x+2)=7x+2?
Show the solution
The checks give 1414 against 22, then 2121 against 99, then 2828 against 1616, all false, so the count is 00​. Distributing shows why, the left side is 7x+147x+14, always 1212 more than 7x+27x+2, so no value of xx closes the gap.
Practice
How many of the values −6−6, −1−1, 66 are solutions of x⋅x=36x⋅x=36?
Show the solution
Both x=−6x=−6 and x=6x=6 work, since (−6)(−6)=36(−6)(−6)=36 and 6⋅6=366⋅6=36, while x=−1x=−1 gives 11, so 22​ of the values are solutions. An equation can have more than one solution, and solving means finding every one of them.
Practice
For 5x−4=3x+15x−4=3x+1, evaluate left side minus right side at x=4x=4.
Show the solution
At x=4x=4 the left side is 5⋅4−4=165⋅4−4=16 and the right side is 3⋅4+1=133⋅4+1=13, so left minus right is 16−13=316−13=3​. The difference is not 00, so 44 is not a solution of the equation.
Practice
For one particular number kk, every one of the values 22, 55, 88, 1111, 1414 is a solution of 5(x+6)=5x+k5(x+6)=5x+k. Enter that kk.
Show the solution
At x=2x=2 the left side is 5⋅8=405⋅8=40 and the right side is 10+k10+k, and the claim is true only when 10+k=4010+k=40, so k=30k=30​. With k=30k=30 the right side is exactly what 5(x+6)5(x+6) distributes to, so the sides are equivalent expressions and every number on the list, along with every other number, is a solution.
